question: True or false: wiping out every death from cancer would lengthen US life expectancy at birth by only about 3 years?
answer: True. Olshansky, Carnes and Cassel calculated in 1990 that eliminating all cancer would add about 3 years to life expectancy at birth. Most cancer deaths come late in life, and the people spared still face a steeply rising risk of dying of something else within a few years.
move: Removing one cause of an outcome leaves the others waiting.
ask: If I solved my biggest worry, which one would take its place?
trap: Counting the lives saved without asking what those people die of next.
reference: Olshansky, Carnes & Cassel, In search of Methuselah: estimating the upper limits to human longevity, Science, 1990
